```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tutorialExtras)
library(gradethis)

#for exercise
library(moderndive)
evals_ch6 <- evals %>%
  select(ID, score, age, gender)

```

## Instructions

Complete this tutorial while reading Sections 6.0 - 6.1 of the [textbook](https://nustat.github.io/intro-stat-data-sci/06-multiple-regression.html). Each question allows 3 'free' attempts. After the third attempt a 10% deduction occurs per attempt.

You can click the "View Grade" button as many times as you would like to see your current grade and the number of attempts you are on. Before submitting make sure your grade is as expected.

### Goals

-   Learn how to perform multiple regression for one numerical & one categorical explanatory variable.
-   Understand the difference between interaction models and parallel slopes models.


## Exercises

Fill in the blank for the code that produces the following plot:

```{r}
htmltools::img(src="images/Figure_06_3.png", height = 400, width = 700)
```

```{r Ex1, exercise=TRUE}
ggplot(evals_ch6, aes(x = ___, y = ___, color = ___)) +
  ____ +
  labs(x = ___, y = ___, color = ___) +
  ___(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```

<div id="Ex1-hint">
**Hint:** Remember to include the parentheses when filling in the blank on line 2.
</div>

```{r Ex1-solution, exercise.reveal_solution = FALSE}
ggplot(evals_ch6, aes(x = age, y = score, color = gender)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "Teaching Score", color = "Gender") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```

```{r Ex1-check}
grade_this_code()
```


## Reading Quiz

```{r Q}
quiz(
  caption = NULL,
  # Q1 (6.1.1)
  question_numeric("Q1) What is the age of the youngest professor in the `evals_ch6` dataset?",
           answer(29, correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q2 (6.1.2)
  question_numeric("Q2) An interaction model with two explanatory variables has the form $\\widehat{y} = b_0 + b_1 \\cdot x_1 + b_2 \\cdot x_2 + b_{1,2} \\cdot x_1 \\cdot x_2$. For `score_model_interaction`, where $x_1$ is age and $x_2$ is gender, what is the value of $b_2$? Round to 3 decimal places.",
           answer(-0.446, correct = TRUE),
           step = 0.001,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q3 (6.1.2)
  question_wordbank("Q3) Consider the following interaction model where age and gender are the explanatory variables, and female is the baseline group for gender. Match each term to its description.\n
$\\widehat{y} = b_0 + b_1 \\cdot \\text{age} + b_2 \\cdot \\mathbb{1}_{\\text{is male}}(x) + b_{1,2} \\cdot \\text{age} \\cdot \\mathbb{1}_{\\text{is male}}(x)$",
           choices = c("\\( b_{0} \\)",
                       "\\( b_{1} \\)",
                       "\\( b_{2} \\)",
                       "\\( b_{1,2} \\)",
                       "\\( b_{0}+b_{2} \\)",
                       "\\( b_{1}+b_{1,2} \\)"),
           wordbank = c("intercept for females", "intercept for males", "offset in intercept for males", "offset in slope of age for males", "slope of age for females", "slope of age for males"),
           answer(c("intercept for females", "slope of age for females", "offset in intercept for males", "offset in slope of age for males", "intercept for males", "slope of age for males"), correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q4 (NEW, 6.1.2)
  question_numeric("Q4) Using `score_model_interaction`, what is the slope for age for the male instructors? Round to 3 decimal places.",
           answer(-0.004, correct = TRUE),
           step = 0.001,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q5 (6.1.2)
  question_numeric("Q5) What is the value of $\\mathbb{1}_{\\text{is male}}(x)$ for the course with `ID` 109 in the `evals_ch6` dataset?",
           answer(0, correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q6 (6.1.2)
  question_numeric("Q6) Consider a model of the form:\n

    y ~ x1 + x2 + x1 * x2

How many quantities does this model estimate? That is, how many values will there be in the Estimate column of a regression table for this model?",
           answer(4, correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q7 (6.1.2)
  question("Q7) Match the model with the appropriate mathematical representation:\n

    lm(score ~ age + gender + age * gender, data = evals_ch6)",
           answer("$\\widehat{y} = b_1 \\cdot x_1 + b_2 \\cdot x_2$"),
           answer("$\\widehat{y} = b_1 \\cdot x_1 + b_2 \\cdot x_2 + b_{1,2} \\cdot x_1 \\cdot x_2$"),
           answer("$\\widehat{y} = b_0 + b_1 \\cdot x_1 + b_2 \\cdot x_2 + b_{1,2} \\cdot x_1 \\cdot x_2$", correct = TRUE),
           answer("$\\widehat{y} = b_0 + b_1 \\cdot x_1 + b_2 \\cdot x_2$"),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q8 (NEW, 6.1.2)
  question("Q8) According to the reading, we say there is an interaction effect if:",
           answer("The associated effect of one variable depends on the value of another variable.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("The two explanatory variables are highly correlated with each other."),
           answer("One explanatory variable causes changes in the other."),
           answer("Both explanatory variables have the same slope."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q9 (NEW, 6.1.3)
  question("Q9) Compared to an interaction model, a parallel slopes model:",
           answer("Allows different intercepts but forces all lines to have the same slope.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Allows different slopes but forces all lines to have the same intercept."),
           answer("Forces all lines to have the same intercept and the same slope."),
           answer("Allows different intercepts and different slopes."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q10 (NEW, 6.1.3)
  question("Q10) Which layer from the `moderndive` package is used to plot a parallel slopes model?",
           answer("`geom_parallel_slopes(se = FALSE)`", correct = TRUE),
           answer("`geom_smooth(method = \"lm\", se = FALSE)`"),
           answer("`geom_point()`"),
           answer("`facet_wrap(~ gender)`"),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q11 (NEW, 6.1.3)
  question_numeric("Q11) Using `score_model_parallel_slopes`, what is the intercept for the male instructors? Round to 3 decimal places.",
           answer(4.675, correct = TRUE),
           step = 0.001,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
  # Q12 (6.1.4)
  question_numeric("Q12) After fitting `score_model_interaction` to the `evals_ch6` dataset, what is the value of $y - \\widehat{y}$ for the 4th course (`ID` = 4)? Round to 3 decimal places.",
           answer(0.548, correct = TRUE),
           step = 0.001,
           allow_retry = TRUE)
)
```
